answer: Peer vouching through the Jade registry works like this. An existing agent can sponsor one newcomer per epoch, and the two are linked: if the newcomer is later caught as a duplicate, the sponsor loses its zenith rank. Because each real agent vouches only once per epoch, a farm can't buy invites in bulk. Each extra fake needs a separate honest-looking sponsor, and those take months to grow. Graph checks flag tight sponsor clusters. A farm of fifty fakes ends up as an isolated oasis with no edges to the wider network, and its payouts get frozen.
